chunks: 4899 - It has been narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم advised ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, saying: “O ʿAlī, when the bride enters your house, remove her shoes when she sits, wash her feet, and pour water from the door of your house to the farthest part of your home. If you do that, Allah will remove from your house seventy thousand kinds of poverty, admit into it seventy thousand kinds of blessing, and send down upon her seventy mercies fluttering over the head of the bride until their blessing reaches every corner of your house. The bride will be safe from insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo so long as she remains in that house. And keep the bride, during her first week, away from milk, vinegar, coriander, and sour apples.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “O Messenger of Allah, for what reason should I keep her from these four things?” He said: “Because the womb becomes barren and cold toward childbearing from these four things, and a mat in a corner of the house is better than a woman who does not give birth.”

Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with vinegar that you forbid it?” He said: “If she menstruates while taking vinegar, she will never become fully pure; coriander stirs menstruation in her belly and makes childbirth difficult for her; and sour apples cut off her menstruation and so become an illness for her.”

Then he said: “O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife at the beginning of the month, its middle, or its end, for insanity, leprosy, and mental disorder may quickly affect her and her child. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife after noon, for if a child is decreed between you at that time, he will be cross-eyed, and Satan rejoices in cross-eyedness in the human being. O ʿAlī, do not speak during intercourse, for if a child is decreed between you, it is feared he may be mute. And let no one look at the private part of his wife; rather let him lower his gaze during intercourse, for looking at the private part causes blindness in the child. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife with desire for another man’s woman, for I fear that if a child is decreed between you, he may be effeminate or feminine and mentally impaired. O ʿAlī, whoever is junub in bed with his wife should not recite the Qur'an, for I fear that a fire may descend upon them from the sky and burn them.”
The compiler of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said: he means by this the recitation of the verses of obligatory prostration, not other than them.

O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife unless you have a cloth and your wife has a cloth, and do not wipe yourselves with one cloth, lest desire fall upon desire, for that leads to enmity between you and then brings you to separation and divorce. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife while standing, for that is from the action of donkeys; and if a child is decreed between you, he will wet the bed like donkeys that urinate everywhere. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife on the night of al-Aḍḥā, for if a child is decreed between you, he will have six fingers or four fingers. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife beneath a fruit-bearing tree, for if a child is decreed between you, he will be a harsh executioner, a killer, or a foreman.”

O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife facing the sun and its brightness unless you lower a covering that conceals you, for if a child is decreed between you, he will remain in misery and poverty until he dies. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife between the adhan and the iqamah, for if a child is decreed between you, he will be eager for the shedding of blood. O ʿAlī, when your wife becomes pregnant, do not have relations with her except while you are in a state of wudu (ablution), for if a child is decreed between you, he will be blind of heart and miserly of hand.”

O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife in the middle of Shaʿbān, for if a child is decreed between you, he will be unfortunate and marked on his face. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife in the final stage of it, when two days remain, for if a child is decreed between you, he will be a tax collector or an aide to the oppressors, and the destruction of groups of people will be at his hands. O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife on the rooftops of buildings, for if a child is decreed between you, he will be a hypocrite, a show-off, and an innovator.”
O ʿAlī, when you go out on a journey, do not have relations with your wife on that night, for if a child is decreed between you, he will spend his wealth in other than what is right.”
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم recited: “Indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils.”
O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife when you leave for a journey of three days and their nights, for if a child is decreed between you, he will be an aide to every oppressor against you.”
O ʿAlī, keep to intercourse on Monday night, for if a child is decreed between you, he will be a preserver of the Book of Allah and content with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has apportioned.”

O ʿAlī, if you have relations with your wife on Tuesday night and a child is decreed between you, he will be granted shahadah after the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah. Allah will not punish him along with the polytheists, and he will have a pleasant scent and mouth, a merciful heart, a generous hand, and a tongue pure from backbiting, lying, and slander.”

O ʿAlī, if you have relations with your wife on Thursday night and a child is decreed between you, he will be a ruler among rulers or a scholar among scholars. And if you have relations with her on Thursday by day when the sun declines from the middle of the sky and a child is decreed between you, Satan will not come near him until he grows old, he will be upright, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will provide him safety in religion and in the world.”

O ʿAlī, if you have relations with her on Friday night and there is a child between you, he will be an orator, eloquent and articulate. And if you have relations with her on Friday after al-ʿAṣr and a child is decreed between you, he will be known, famous, and learned. And if you have relations with her on Friday night after the last ʿIshāʾ, then it is hoped that the child will be among the abdāl, if Allah the Exalted wills.”

O ʿAlī, do not have relations with your wife in the first hour of the night, for if a child is decreed between you, it is feared he may be a sorcerer preferring the world over the Hereafter. O ʿAlī, preserve this counsel of mine just as I preserved it from Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام.”

key_terms.الرَّحِمَ: the womb in the context of childbearing
key_terms.الشَّهَادَةَ: martyrdom, mentioned as a possible virtue for offspring
key_terms.الْأَبْدَالِ: the abdāl, a class of righteous servants hoped for in the offspring
key_terms.الْبَرَكَةِ: divine blessing placed in the household
key_terms.الْعَرُوسُ: the bride entering the husband’s home
key_terms.الْعَزَائِمِ: the Qur'anic verses of obligatory prostration
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), ritual purity before intercourse in one case mentioned

ai.seo_question: What advice did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم give Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام about marriage, intimacy, and household etiquette?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a lengthy وصيّة from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning marriage, intimacy, household blessing, and spousal etiquette. It combines recommendations, cautions, and spiritual-moral instructions tied to times, conditions, and conduct within married life, and includes a Qur'anic citation regarding wastefulness.
